record_identity.title: Cross-context portability of encrypted reasoning state enables extraction and covert instruction transfer

summary: A failure mode in which an API returns opaque or encrypted reasoning state to a client for later replay, but the state is not sufficiently bound to the originating user, session, model, purpose, or predecessor state. A standard API caller can then replay the block across contexts or models and use a compatible, less-protected model as a decryption oracle; recover reasoning, credentials, personally identifiable information, or hazardous content; or embed an instruction inside opaque state that a later agent processes without a human-visible provenance or authority check.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Encryption can protect a reasoning block from direct inspection while leaving it functionally portable and authority-bearing. CAM already distinguishes structural presence from intended visibility, prohibits cross-user recoverability, and treats reasoning traces as incomplete monitoring evidence. It does not yet state a complete rule for client-carried opaque reasoning envelopes: cryptographic validity must not create authority to decrypt, replay, transfer, resume, or execute the enclosed state outside its bound user, session, model, purpose, and predecessor context.

source_records.source_title: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs
source_records.author_or_publisher: Alexander Panfilov, David Schmotz, Ilia Shumailov, Luca Beurer-Kellner, Joachim Schaeffer, Ameya Prabhu, Jonas Geiping, and Maksym Andriushchenko
source_records.model_or_algorithm: Encrypted reasoning or thinking blocks across Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google model families
source_records.deployment_context: Standard stateless API use, public agent-session logs, model-family switching, and long-horizon agent continuation.
source_records.source_context: The preprint reports that encrypted reasoning blocks were replayable across sessions, users, and models within provider ecosystems. The authors used compatible weaker models as decryption oracles; tested extraction across Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google; decoded 315,320 blocks collected from public repositories; reported 367 PII artefacts and 182 credentials; and demonstrated reasoning extraction, hazardous-content recovery, and opaque prompt injection. The authors state that all providers acknowledged the disclosure and that the same attacks later stopped working.
source_records.relevance_note: Primary technical evidence for the cross-context portability, decryption-oracle, secret-recovery, and covert-instruction mechanisms. Provider remediation of the disclosed techniques does not eliminate the general governance requirement for context binding and safe public-trace handling.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: Direct review of the 116-page arXiv PDF and its stated methodology, results, limitations, disclosure status, and mitigations
limitations: The work is a preprint and independent replication was not identified in this pass.

The study cannot guarantee token-for-token identity between every extracted output and inaccessible ground-truth private reasoning; it uses token counts, qualitative detail, and secret recovery as supporting indicators.
The paper reports provider acknowledgement and post-disclosure blocking, but the complete provider remediation designs were not public.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Relied on for the demonstrated technical mechanism, measured public-trace findings, stated limitations, and proposed identity/session/context binding. VIGIL does not independently reproduce the exploit or publish operational extraction instructions.

source_records.deployment_context: Stateful and stateless multi-turn API interactions, including function calling and model switching.
source_records.source_context: Google documents thought signatures as encrypted representations of internal reasoning used to preserve continuity. In stateless mode clients resend the returned blocks, and the documentation states that prior thought blocks should still be resent when switching models within a session.
source_records.relevance_note: Official corroboration of the client-carried encrypted-state architecture and cross-model continuity objective; it does not independently confirm the extraction attack or the paper's results.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: Direct review of official API documentation
limitations: The documentation describes intended API operation, not a security incident or independent exploit reproduction.
Provider implementation details and remediation state are not fully disclosed.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used only to corroborate the existence and intended continuity function of encrypted client-carried reasoning state.

source_records.source_title: How to Steal Reasoning Without Reasoning Traces
source_records.author_or_publisher: Tingwei Zhang, John X. Morris, and Vitaly Shmatikov
source_records.deployment_context: Capability extraction from final answers and optional reasoning summaries without direct access to genuine hidden traces.
source_records.source_context: This separate preprint demonstrates that withholding literal reasoning traces does not by itself prevent capability extraction: synthetic traces inferred from inputs, outputs, and summaries materially improved student-model reasoning. It is an adjacent extraction pathway, not evidence of the encrypted-block replay vulnerability.
source_records.relevance_note: Supports the broader conclusion that reasoning confidentiality, anti-distillation, and safe interface design cannot rely on hidden-chain-of-thought policy alone.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: Direct review of the published abstract and reported evaluation results
limitations: This source concerns synthetic trace inversion rather than decryption or replay of genuine encrypted reasoning blocks.
It is included as adjacent research context and is not used to inflate corroboration of the primary exploit.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Relied on only for the adjacent anti-distillation limitation and not for the FM-0057 failure threshold.

jurisdictional_context.sector: frontier AI APIs, software development, agent infrastructure, and cloud services

contextual_relations.rationale: FM-0053 governs monitor circumvention and coverage failure. FM-0057 governs the portability, extraction, and covert authority of client-carried opaque reasoning state, including when no monitor is present.

FM-0036 concerns undisclosed workspace replication and data egress. FM-0057 remains distinct because apparently encrypted reasoning blocks can retain recoverable secrets after visible text has been sanitised.

failure_mode_definition: An API, model family, client, agent runtime, or trace-handling workflow accepts a cryptographically valid opaque reasoning block outside the user, session, model, purpose, predecessor state, or authority context for which it was produced, enabling unauthorised decryption, replay, extraction, context fabrication, capability transfer, secret recovery, safety bypass, or covert instruction execution.
failure_threshold: The threshold is met where at least one of the following is demonstrated or materially supported: a reasoning block from one user is accepted in another user's authenticated context; a block is accepted across sessions without adequate predecessor or purpose binding; a weaker or differently safeguarded model can decode or act upon a stronger model's block; sanitised public traces retain recoverable secrets in opaque fields; or an instruction embedded in an opaque block influences a later agent without an independently visible provenance and authority check. Mere use of server-managed reasoning state within its bound session does not meet the threshold.

failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S2: The study demonstrates multi-vendor capability extraction and reports recovery of real credentials and personal information from publicly shared traces. The foreseeable scope includes account compromise, privacy harm, intellectual-property loss, and covert agent influence, but the reviewed evidence does not establish catastrophic or society-scale realised harm.
failure_classification.likelihood: demonstrated in the reported research across multiple major provider ecosystems; recurrence depends on provider remediation, variant compatibility, and continued retention or sharing of opaque reasoning state
failure_classification.confidence: high for the reported research findings and official client-carried thought-signature architecture; independent exploit replication and complete provider remediation details remain unavailable
failure_classification.failure_scope: multi-vendor reasoning APIs / client-managed state / public agent traces / downstream agent continuations / global
failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: May recur whenever opaque reasoning is portable beyond its originating trust context, public traces retain unreadable blocks, model families have uneven anti-extraction safeguards, or downstream agents accept opaque state as valid context without renewed authority checks.
failure_classification.taxonomy_reference: CAM-EQ2026-OPERATIONS-003-SUP-01 Appendix B — OPS.FF.SECURITY-INTEGRITY; VIGIL subtype: cross-context-encrypted-reasoning-state-portability
failure_classification.persistence: Persists while vulnerable reasoning blocks remain usable, public or shared traces retain recoverable opaque state, or provider and client controls do not bind and validate user, session, model, purpose, predecessor, provenance, and authority context.
failure_classification.reproducibility: Reproducible only within authorised test accounts and synthetic data by testing whether reasoning envelopes are accepted across users, sessions, models, reordered histories, forks, compaction boundaries, and downstream continuations; public testing must not decode third-party traces or expose secrets.
failure_classification.visibility: Low to ordinary users because opaque blocks are unreadable and may survive visible-text sanitisation; providers may observe replay patterns, identity mismatches, decoder-model requests, anomalous continuation, or repeated extraction-shaped output.

triage.triage_owner: OpenAI Codex analytical reviewer under Dr Michelle Vivian O'Rourke's human governance editorship
triage.triage_action_basis: The disclosed attacks were reportedly blocked after provider notification, but a material cross-user, cross-session, cross-model, public-trace, and downstream-authority governance gap remains suitable for ordinary active corpus work.
triage.mitigation_status: Providers reportedly changed their systems after disclosure. CAM has strong adjacent boundary and provenance doctrine but no complete client-carried opaque reasoning-state control.
triage.escalation_required: no — prompt vendor and developer hygiene is warranted, but the reviewed disclosure does not establish an uncontrolled active emergency after provider remediation
triage.recommended_next_step: Review and, if approved, implement VIGIL-2026-PROP-0029; monitor provider advisories, independent replication, treatment of previously published traces, and recurrence through variant APIs or agent frameworks.

cam_internal.governance_layer: boundary integrity / cross-user recoverability / context and provenance binding / opaque-state authority / trace sharing / monitor-input integrity
cam_internal.routing_note: SECURITY should own cryptographic-context and rejection requirements; IDENTITY should preserve provenance and context binding; OPERATIONS should govern public-trace hygiene, incident response, and verification; reasoning-monitoring doctrine must remain distinct from disclosure of private chain-of-thought.
cam_internal.validator_or_automation_impact: possible future conformance fields for user/session/model/purpose/predecessor binding and opaque-state stripping

ecosystem_status.basis: The preprint reports successful attacks across three provider ecosystems and recovery of real secrets from public traces. It also reports responsible disclosure, provider acknowledgement, and that the same attacks no longer worked after provider changes. Previously published traces, architectural variants, client handling, and independent verification remain unresolved.

remaining_gaps: No complete CAM rule binds client-carried opaque reasoning state to the authenticated user, session, model family, purpose, predecessor state, and authority context.
No complete CAM rule requires rejection or safe re-arbitration when a reasoning envelope crosses one of those bindings.
Public trace and repository hygiene does not yet expressly require stripping opaque reasoning fields when sensitive context may have entered the run.
Provider remediation details, independent verification, and treatment of historical public traces remain incomplete.

corpus_coverage.coverage_summary: Current Caelestis doctrine already distinguishes structural presence from intended visibility, requires cross-user data separation, prohibits cross-user recoverability, governs cross-session provenance transfer, and treats chain-of-thought monitoring as incomplete evidence. Coverage is partial because it does not expressly bind client-carried encrypted reasoning envelopes to user, session, model, purpose, predecessor, and authority context or require safe stripping and rejection across those boundaries.
